articles.title: How engineers in a WhatsApp group are guiding Nepal’s flood rescue efforts
articles.summary: A WhatsApp group of over 500 engineers has become a critical hub for Nepal's flood rescue operations. The engineers share technical drawings, advice, and information about missing workers to help rescue teams navigate and search buried hydropower tunnels. Their rapid coordination and expertise are improving the efficiency of rescue efforts amid the ongoing disaster.

articles.title: Nepal unveils relief package to help flood-hit businesses recover
articles.summary: The Nepalese government announced a comprehensive relief package aimed at helping businesses devastated by the recent Bhotekoshi floods. The measures include customs and tax exemptions, restructuring of existing loans, and the provision of cheaper credit facilities. The package is intended to accelerate recovery, preserve jobs, and stabilize local economies in the flood‑affected districts. Officials say the assistance will be coordinated through the Ministry of Finance and relevant financial institutions, with priority given to small and medium enterprises that suffered the greatest losses.

articles.title: Nepal flood survivors pulled alive from hydropower tunnel nine days later
articles.summary: Two men trapped in the Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel were rescued nine days after the August 26 flood disaster that caused the tunnel to collapse. Rescuers heard voices inside the tunnel, prompting a focused search that led to the successful extraction of the survivors. The rescue raises hope that other victims may still be alive, though the overall situation remains dire with ongoing recovery efforts after the flood that devastated parts of Nepal.

articles.title: Wife says rescued husband has ‘a second life’ after nine days trapped in Nepal tunnel
articles.summary: After being trapped for nine days inside the Trishuli 3A tunnel, Kabir Maharjan was rescued on Friday. His wife, Hira Shobha, expressed relief and described her husband as having a "second life" following the ordeal. The family had endured a painful period believing he might still be alive inside the tunnel before rescuers finally pulled him out. The incident highlights the dangers of tunnel work in Nepal and the dedication of rescue teams.

articles.title: Rescued tunnel worker says he stayed behind to save others
articles.summary: Tunnel worker Sanjay Sah was rescued after being trapped for nine days in the Trishuli 3A tunnel when a flood hit the structure. Sah told rescuers he deliberately delayed his own escape to assist fellow workers in fleeing the inundated tunnel, demonstrating self‑sacrifice. His rescue highlights both the dangers faced by infrastructure projects in Nepal during extreme weather and the bravery of individuals involved.

articles.title: How two Nepal hydropower workers survived nine days trapped underground
articles.summary: Two workers at a Nepalese hydropower project were trapped underground for nine days after a sudden flood. One worker stayed behind to assist his colleagues in escaping the rising water, while the other had arrived for routine maintenance. Both survived the ordeal, emerging after a lengthy rescue operation that highlighted the risks faced by workers in remote infrastructure projects.

articles.title: Prime Minister Balendra Shah, Australia’s Anthony Albanese discuss flood response
articles.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese discussed Nepal's recent flood disaster, with Shah thanking Australia for its rescue and relief assistance. Shah announced that Nepal is intensifying efforts to locate Australians reported missing after the floods, highlighting ongoing bilateral cooperation in disaster response.

articles.title: Nepal flood death toll reaches 1,287
articles.summary: The death toll from recent floods in Nepal has risen to 1,287, with bodies recovered in eight districts. Chitwan district reported the highest number of fatalities at 359, followed by Nawalparasi East and Nawalparasi West. The disaster has caused widespread loss of life across the affected regions.

articles.title: Nepal home minister tells critics to focus on results, not where he works
articles.summary: Home Minister Sudan Gurung responded to social media criticism over his involvement in the recent flood response and the rescue operation in a tunnel on Friday. While some netizens questioned why the minister was present at the site, Gurung defended his role, emphasizing that the focus should be on the outcomes of the rescue and relief efforts rather than his physical presence. He highlighted the coordination work being done by his ministry and urged critics to prioritize results over speculation about his whereabouts.

articles.title: Search and rescue team says ‘no more survivors in Upper Trishuli 3A tunnel’
articles.summary: Rescue teams working in the Upper Trishuli 3A tunnel have announced that after rescuing two survivors and recovering one deceased, no additional survivors or bodies have been found. The operation, which followed a tunnel collapse, concluded that the likelihood of finding more victims is now nil. Authorities continue to assess the incident's cause and provide support to the families of those affected.

articles.title: US probes Iran wedding strike that analysis shows was likely direct hit by US munition
articles.summary: Iranian state television reported that a 22‑year‑old woman died in hospital after a strike hit a home during a wedding, bringing the death toll to five. The United States has opened a probe into the incident, with analysis indicating it was likely a direct hit by U.S. munition. The investigation will examine the circumstances and accountability for the attack that occurred in Iran.

articles.title: Road department begins cutting new track to reopen flood-hit Prithvi Highway
articles.summary: The Nepalese Road Department has started cutting a new 50‑metre temporary track to bypass the Krishnabhir landslide that blocked the Prithvi Highway after recent floods. The work involves widening a temporary route around the affected area to restore traffic flow on this crucial national artery.

articles.title: The mountains have changed. Nepal must too
articles.summary: The article warns that the Himalayas are undergoing rapid transformation due to climate change, glacial retreat, and increased landslide risk. It argues that Nepal must adapt by establishing a resilient mountain monitoring system that integrates satellite data, remote‑sensing technology, on‑ground field investigations, weather forecasting, river flow monitoring, and indigenous local knowledge. Such a comprehensive approach would improve early warning capabilities, guide disaster risk reduction, and inform sustainable development policies in the mountainous regions.

articles.title: Nvidia donates $10 million to flood recovery, one of Nepal’s biggest corporate donations
articles.summary: Nvidia has pledged a $10 million donation to Nepal’s flood recovery efforts, marking one of the largest corporate contributions in the country’s history. The funds have been transferred to the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund and were motivated by the initiative of over 50 Nepali employees working for the US technology firm. The donation aims to support rebuilding infrastructure, providing relief supplies, and aiding affected communities after the recent devastating floods.

articles.title: Five of 15 drinking water sources in flood-hit Bidur contaminated with E. coli
articles.summary: In the flood‑stricken town of Bidur, Nepal, tests have found that five of the fifteen drinking‑water sources are contaminated with E. coli. Health officials are responding by planning a cholera vaccination campaign targeting roughly 100,000 people deemed most vulnerable, and a measles immunisation drive for over 75,000 children. The contamination highlights the public‑health risks posed by the recent floods and the urgent need for clean water and disease prevention measures.

articles.title: Why climate change is a threat to Nepal’s hydropower sector
articles.summary: The article warns that climate change is already endangering Nepal’s hydropower industry, with the recent August monsoon disaster illustrating the severity of the threat. It explains how altered rainfall patterns, intensified floods, and glacial melt are disrupting river flows, damaging infrastructure, and jeopardizing future energy generation. Experts and officials call for urgent adaptation measures, improved dam design, and integrated water management to safeguard the sector that underpins Nepal’s economic growth and energy security.

articles.title: Why Nepal must demand climate reparations
articles.summary: Nepal demands climate reparations from the Global North for historical ecological debts.

articles.title: After nine days in darkness, two men walked back into the light
articles.summary: Rescuers have successfully retrieved Sanjay Sah and Kabir Maharjan alive from the Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel after more than 72 hours of intensive search. The two men survived nine days in complete darkness before being brought back to the surface. While their rescue is a relief, dozens of other workers remain missing, and the full extent of the incident is still being investigated. Authorities continue to search the tunnel, and families await news on the unaccounted individuals.

articles.title: Can Nepal turn Himalayan vulnerability into a case for compensation?
articles.summary: The recent Bhotekoshi flood disaster underscores the growing climate vulnerability of Nepal's Himalayan region. While the event highlights the urgent need for adaptation and compensation mechanisms, experts argue that Nepal must first gather robust scientific evidence of climate‑induced damages, develop a focused diplomatic approach, and craft a clear strategy to attract international climate finance and compensation grants. Without these steps, the country risks missing opportunities to secure the support needed to rebuild and protect vulnerable communities.

articles.title: Barely saved, he cuts mourning short to help flood survivors
articles.summary: Sudip Kumar Neupane survived a devastating flood on the Trishuli River that claimed the lives of his younger brother and a close colleague. After two days of mourning, he chose to cut short his period of grief to assist other flood survivors, coordinating relief efforts and providing aid. The tragedy highlights the ongoing vulnerability of communities along Nepal's rivers during the monsoon season, as rescue teams continue to search for missing persons and distribute essential supplies. Neupane's swift shift from personal loss to community service underscores the resilience and solidarity among Nepalese citizens facing natural disasters.

articles.title: They stopped hoping to find him alive. Then they found a hand
articles.summary: Raj Kumar Diyali disappeared along with his wife and four‑year‑old son during the devastating Bhotekoshi flood in Nepal. After days of searching, rescuers recovered a hand, raising hopes of locating the missing family members. The relatives are now awaiting DNA testing to confirm the identity of the recovered remains. The incident highlights the ongoing challenges faced by communities affected by the flood and the emotional toll on families awaiting closure.

articles.title: Where to support flood relief in Kathmandu this week and beyond
articles.summary: The article lists a series of events taking place in Kathmandu this week and beyond that aim to raise funds and awareness for communities affected by recent floods. Options include charity runs, creative workshops, art exhibitions, and donation drives organized by local NGOs, the Kathmandu Metropolitan City, and international agencies. Participants can contribute by registering for events, purchasing artwork, or making direct donations. The piece highlights how these activities not only provide immediate relief but also foster community resilience and long‑term recovery.

articles.title: ‘Tiniharu’ lifts the fog around those at margins
articles.summary: Abinash Bikram Shah’s debut film “Tiniharu,” which won an award at Cannes, centers on a Kinnar (transgender) family in Nepal. The narrative explores themes of belonging, othering, and the fragile limits of societal acceptance, shedding light on the lives of those living at the margins. By bringing the Kinnar experience to an international platform, the film challenges stereotypes and invites viewers to reconsider notions of identity and inclusion.

articles.title: 27 US lawmakers urge Rubio to expand rescue, aid efforts in Nepal
articles.summary: A group of 27 U.S. lawmakers have written to Senator Marco Rubio urging the expansion of American disaster response capabilities in Nepal following a major earthquake that left thousands missing. The letter requests the deployment of a U.S. disaster response team, high‑altitude search and rescue assets, and faster assistance to support Nepalese authorities. Lawmakers emphasize the urgency of coordinated international aid and highlight the humanitarian crisis unfolding in the region.

articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to address UN General Assembly on September 24
articles.summary: Nepal PM Balendra Shah will address the UN General Assembly on September 24, his first foreign trip since taking office, as Nepal seeks international support after devastating floods.
